description:
Every remaining test in the gate's suite whose verdict a busy host can flip is decided on what the code did instead, so no assertion in the authoritative gate turns on how promptly a thread was scheduled.

## Background

`57675b68`'s survey of the whole `cargo-ci` suite recorded four sites it did not close, each the shape that issue removed — a wall-clock wait deciding a test that is about ordering — at a wider margin. The container's REQ-03 names their subject, so they are its remainder rather than follow-up work.

Three are the same shape. `test_second_thread_waits_for_the_holder` in `crates/jit/src/storage/repo_lock.rs` gives a contender a five-second wait against a 150-millisecond hold and unwraps the result: the ordering assertion beside it is decided by the lock and is sound, but the unwrap turns a five-second stall into a failure about scheduling. `test_session_disjoint_sessions_serialize_on_worktree_bootstrap` in `crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store_tests.rs` reads identically. `test_execute_waits_for_competing_repository_write_guard` in `crates/jit/src/commands/archive.rs` requires the archive to complete within two seconds of the guard being released; joining the worker before receiving removes the wait, because a finished thread has already sent.

The fourth is a cluster rather than a site. `crates/jit/src/storage/lease.rs` builds leases with a one-second TTL and asserts staleness against a one-second threshold, then reasons across sleeps of 100 to 900 milliseconds. Each of those assertions holds only while the process stays inside the remaining fraction of a second. `Lease` reads `Instant::now()` and `Utc::now()` directly, so the restatement is an injected clock rather than a change to the tests: `ClaimCoordinator` already takes one, and `crates/jit/src/storage/clock.rs` is the mechanism it takes.

The fourth site turned out to be dead code: `crates/jit/src/storage/lease.rs` declares a `Lease` superseded by `claim_coordinator::Lease`, which is what `storage::Lease` re-exports, and nothing in the workspace reaches the older one. Injecting a clock into it would produce clock-injected dead code and leave a duplicate representation of a canonical type standing, which `@/invariant/canonical-cutover` calls a defect. The owner ruled the module deleted instead, and REQ-03 asks for the end state rather than for the injection.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The lock-contention properties in `repo_lock.rs` and `repository_state_store_tests.rs` are decided by what the lock did. A bound that fires only when nothing the wait watches has progressed, and fails loudly naming what it last saw, is permitted.
- [hard] REQ-02: The archive test reaches its result without a wall-clock wait for it.
- [hard] REQ-03: No assertion about lease expiry or staleness depends on the process reaching it inside a fraction of a second.
- [hard] REQ-04: Each property still fails when the behaviour it protects genuinely breaks, demonstrated against a seeded regression.
- [hard] REQ-05: A re-run of the gate-suite survey reports every remaining assertion a busy host can flip, retained bounds included, each with the argument for its retention; its result is stated.
title: Decide the gate suite's remaining timed tests on behaviour, not on scheduling
